annotations.text:
CHH-F04 — Proximity Notifications (US-CHH-004-01/03/04/05)
Flow: Blood Request Form -> matching -> Donor Notification Center -> Request Details (accept or decline) -> Requester Dashboard.
US-CHH-004-02 is the backend matching engine and has no UI.
Every screen now ships mobile AND web. Every artboard carries an AC-state tweak; the two dashboards also carry a viewer tweak (registered / guest).

Decisions settled in this revision — all three were open points before:
1. ACCEPT IS GREEN. New token family --go (#3F6B39, 6.2:1 on white) added to design/component-gallery.html and documented in design/ui-standard.md as the standard positive/accept action, with the b-accept button variant. It is distinct from --blood (emergency and destructive) and from --leaf (status green: verified, eligible, success toast). Decline stays neutral secondary, never red.
2. URGENCY IS Emergency / Urgent / Standard everywhere — request form, cards, push, SMS, dashboard. The story's High/Normal wording is dropped.
3. REQUEST LIFETIME IS 6 HOURS from creation to auto-expiry. Shown as a labelled countdown plus a life bar on both dashboards, as 'Request closes in' on both request-details screens, and as 'Closes in ...' on the notification cards. Copy names the rule in words the first time it matters.

BUSINESS RULE — donor-list visibility (new, applies to Dashboard and DashboardWeb; use the 'viewer' tweak to compare).

Guest requester (unregistered session): the list shows ONLY donors who have reached Accepted. Pending / sent / viewed donors are not listed at all — not even as locked placeholder rows. Aggregate reassurance ('38 more donors were notified') is allowed; a per-donor trace is not.

Registered requester: the list shows EVERY matched donor, anonymised as Donor 1, Donor 2, Donor 3... in stable match order, each unaccepted row carrying one flat 'Pending' label. No Sent / Viewed / Opened / Declined on any row — delivery telemetry about a named individual invites exactly the pressure this product must not create. The aggregate stats were reduced to Notified / Yet to respond / Accepted to stay consistent with that.

Both: accepting is what reveals a real name and number, and nothing before it does. The ordinal is stable for the life of the request.

For Confluence on merge: add 1) request lifetime = 6 hours, 2) this visibility rule, to the story's Business Rules field.

OFF-APP DELIVERY — push and SMS carry the same four facts in the same order: blood group and units, urgency (one of the three words), approximate distance, area. Never the patient name, the requester's identity, an exact address or a reason for the transfusion — these land on lock screens anyone standing nearby can read.

SMS is the fallback for donors with push disabled and the only channel for a donor with no app. It has no buttons, so the donor answers with a keyword: 'Reply YES to accept, NO to decline.' Under 160 characters so it sends as one segment; a YES is answered with the requester's name and number (same reveal-on-acceptance rule as the app) plus the closing time, since an SMS donor has no countdown to look at; a NO is acknowledged once and ends the thread.

Where the OS allows notification actions, push carries Accept (green) and Decline side by side.
